text:
#MediaTek is a leading global supplier of smartphone SoCs and has extended its low-power design, connectivity, and high-volume manufacturing capabilities into smart automotive systems, AI PCs, and smart home devices. With its technologies powering more than 2 billion connected devices annually, MediaTek has become an important platform for edge computing while also expanding into the custom AI ASIC market.

#NVIDIA is deepening its capital, product roadmap, and supply chain collaboration with MediaTek through an investment in $3.5 billion of MediaTek’s convertible bonds. In data centers, the two companies are developing customized XPUs through NVLink Fusion. In personal computing, they are integrating NVIDIA GPUs with MediaTek SoCs across GB10, DGX Spark, and RTX Spark platforms. In automotive applications, the companies are combining MediaTek’s Dimensity Auto with NVIDIA’s RTX and DRIVE platforms.

The partnership could create a connected ecosystem spanning cloud training, edge inference, and end-device interaction. Models can be trained on NVIDIA GPUs and within #NVLink AI Factory infrastructure before being deployed across the PCs, vehicles, and smart devices powered by MediaTek. Data and usage scenarios collected at the edge can then feed back into cloud-based model optimization. This would expand the reach of NVIDIA’s #CUDA, #RTX, and NVLink ecosystems, while enabling MediaTek to evolve from a consumer-chip supplier into a broader platform company spanning custom ASICs, AI PCs, and intelligent vehicles.

text:
NVIDIA 2Q Revenue Surges 106% YoY; FY2028 Revenue Expected to Grow 70%
NVIDIA announced its fiscal 2Q27 results on August 26, reporting record revenue of $96.22 billion, up 106% YoY. Data Center revenue reached $89.02B, surging 117% YoY and serving as the company’s primary growth engine. Looking ahead, NVIDIA expects third-quarter revenue to reach approximately $108B. CFO Colette Kress said during the earnings call that FY2028 revenue is expected to grow by around 70%, with the outlook constrained primarily by supply chain capacity rather than a lack of market demand.

Vera Rubin Platform Enters Full Production
Commenting on current market developments, NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang said AI has reached an inflection point, with the technology now capable of performing useful work and generating productive, economically valuable tokens. He emphasized that the global AI infrastructure buildout is advancing at full speed, while NVIDIA’s latest Vera Rubin platform has entered full-scale production.
Huang added that companies will eventually operate multiple AI agents on a continuous basis, potentially driving a 15- to 100-fold increase in overall computing requirements.

Gross Margins Face Downward Pressure
Despite maintaining a strong gross margin of 75% in the second quarter, NVIDIA is expected to face mounting cost pressures. Kress noted that surging AI demand has tightened memory supply, with extreme pricing conditions exceeding the company’s previous expectations and likely to persist through next year.
NVIDIA has therefore lowered its gross margin outlook. The company expects gross margin to decline to 74% in the third quarter and bottom out at 71–72% in the fourth quarter before recovering to 72–73% in the first quarter of FY2028.

Huang Addresses Circular Financing Concerns
NVIDIA’s substantial investments in frontier AI labs have raised market concerns over so-called “circular financing.” Kress acknowledged these concerns but said NVIDIA views these labs as once-in-a-century companies, with limited investment risk and attractive potential returns. AI labs requiring balance-sheet support are expected to account for approximately one-quarter of NVIDIA’s business next year.
Huang added that NVIDIA provides a complete AI factory platform that is fundamentally different from custom inference chips designed for individual functions. He expressed confidence in NVIDIA’s technology and expects these AI labs to remain significant long-term users of the company’s computing architecture.

#HBF is emerging as a complementary technology to #HBM rather than a competing one, with the potential to address HBM's high cost and limited capacity. While HBM delivers unmatched memory bandwidth, it is difficult for it alone to meet the massive capacity requirements of #LLM inference. HBF, on the other hand, leverages stacked Flash technology to provide sufficient bandwidth while offering several times the memory capacity of HBM at a significantly lower cost.

Although #NVIDIA has yet to announce any plans to adopt the technology, industry sentiment remains broadly positive. The interest shown by industry leaders such as #Google and #Tenstorrent have shown a willingness to consider adopting HBF, though specific use cases have not yet been determined.  #TrendForce believes the long-term architecture will likely combine HBM for ultra-high-speed computation with HBF for high-density data storage, creating a hybrid memory hierarchy that could become a key enabler of large-scale AI commercialization.

AI Infrastructure Begins Delivering Returns as Big Tech Posts Strong 2Q26 Results

Financial results for the quarter that ended on June 30, 2026 underscore that artificial intelligence has become the primary engine of revenue growth across the global technology sector. Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft all reported robust double-digit growth in their cloud and AI businesses. Management teams consistently emphasized that years of aggressive AI infrastructure investment are now translating into tangible commercial returns, while also creating new monetization opportunities, including the potential commercialization of excess AI computing capacity.

#Amazon: AWS Delivers Fastest Growth in 18 Quarters as AI and Chip Businesses Surpass $25B Run Rate

Amazon reported net sales of $200.6B, up 20% YoY. Driven by strong AI demand, AWS generated $42.2B in revenue, representing 37% YoY growth. CEO Andy Jassy noted that AWS recorded its fastest growth in 18 quarters, with revenue increasing 36.7% during the quarter. He also revealed that both Amazon's AI business and custom silicon business have each surpassed an annualized revenue run rate of $25B, highlighting the company's successful expansion across AI services and in-house chip development.

#Alphabet: Cloud Business Accelerates as AI Deepens Enterprise Adoption
Alphabet delivered another standout quarter, with revenue reaching $119.8B, up 24% YoY. Google Cloud revenue surged 82% YoY to $24.8B, fueled by strong enterprise demand for AI infrastructure and cloud-based AI solutions. CEO Sundar Pichai said the company's AI investments are reshaping every part of its business and noted that Gemini Enterprise has now been adopted by nearly 90% of Fortune 100 companies, underscoring the growing enterprise adoption of Google's end-to-end AI platform.

#Meta: AI Strengthens Core Business as Compute Capacity Emerges as a New Monetization Opportunity

Meta generated $60.8B in revenue during the quarter, an increase of 28% YoY. Net income declined 14% YoY to $15.8B due to a $2.4B legal settlement charge, although the company's core advertising business remained strong, with ad impressions rising 14%.
During the earnings call, CEO Mark Zuckerberg confirmed that Meta is actively evaluating the commercialization of excess AI computing capacity by leasing it to third parties. He noted that the company has already received numerous offers for its compute resources at prices carrying a significant premium over Meta's acquisition cost, highlighting a potentially meaningful new revenue stream as AI infrastructure continues to scale.

#Microsoft: Cloud Business Continues to Expand as Copilot Accelerates Enterprise AI Adoption

For the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 that ended on June 30, 2026, Microsoft reported revenue of $90B, up 18% YoY. Microsoft Cloud revenue reached $59.3B, representing 27% YoY growth, while Azure and other cloud services grew 43% YoY.
CEO Satya Nadella emphasized Microsoft's focus on improving the economics of AI deployment, stating that the company is pushing the frontier of the cost-performance curve to help customers convert AI tokens into measurable business outcomes. He also revealed that Azure's annual revenue surpassed $100B for the first time, while paid seats for Microsoft 365 Copilot exceeded 30 million, demonstrating strong enterprise adoption of Microsoft's AI offerings.

The company also significantly expanded shipments of HBM4 and delivered samples of the industry's first HBM4E to major customers, further reinforcing its technology leadership in next-generation AI memory.

In addition, Samsung's foundry business reported improved profitability, supported by strong orders from U.S. customers and growing demand for HBM base dies. The company also continued securing 2nm HPC design wins, strengthening its advanced foundry pipeline.

In contrast to the strong performance of the semiconductor business, Samsung's Device eXperience (DX) division, which includes smartphones and consumer electronics, faced mounting cost pressures. Quarterly revenue declined 9% sequentially.

Within the DX division, the Mobile eXperience (MX) business reported ₩33.2T in revenue and an operating loss of ₩0.7T, primarily due to industry-wide increases in component costs that weighed on profitability.

TrendForce notes that while AI infrastructure investment continues to drive robust demand for high-value memory products such as HBM and server DRAM, rising component costs are increasingly pressuring consumer electronics manufacturers. This divergence highlights the widening performance gap between AI-driven semiconductor businesses and consumer-facing hardware segments.

Cumulative first-half revenue also exceeded ₩100T for the first time.

SK hynix attributed its strong performance to continued price increases for both DRAM and NAND Flash, alongside robust demand for high-value-added products, including HBM, AI server DRAM, and enterprise SSDs (eSSDs). As AI continues evolving toward Agentic AI and becomes increasingly integrated across a broad range of services, the company expects memory demand to broaden beyond AI-specific applications, creating a structural growth trend in both AI-oriented and mainstream memory markets.

On the DRAM front, SK hynix further strengthened its leadership in HBM. The company's HBM4, offering industry-leading power efficiency and cost competitiveness, entered mass production during the second quarter, with production scheduled to expand further in the second half of the year. Customer samples of HBM4E were also successfully delivered during the first half of 2026. Additionally, SOCAMM2, manufactured using the company's sixth-generation 10nm-class (1c) process technology, officially entered volume shipments and recorded strong sales growth during the quarter.

In the NAND Flash business, 321L QLC products have become the company's highest-volume NAND offering. SK hynix aims to increase the proportion of 321L QLC production at its Korean manufacturing facilities to approximately 50% by the end of 2026, further optimizing its product mix toward higher-performance, higher-value storage solutions.

TrendForce previously noted that major memory suppliers continue prioritizing capital expenditure toward DRAM expansion, leaving NAND Flash capacity additions relatively limited. As a result, NAND supply growth in 2026 has primarily been driven by process technology migration rather than significant capacity expansion, keeping market supply relatively tight without signs of substantial oversupply. 

Looking ahead to 2027, suppliers in South Korea, the U.S., and Japan are expected to continue advancing process technologies while gradually bringing new capacity online. Meanwhile, Chinese manufacturers are projected to further expand production as additional equipment enters operation, with China's share of global NAND Flash supply expected to approach 19%. TrendForce expects the NAND Flash market to gradually rebalance in 2H27 as new capacity ramps throughout the industry, easing the current supply tightness.

text:
TSMC Delivers Strong 2Q26 Results as 2nm Process Contributes Revenue for the First Time

TSMC reported strong results for 2Q26, driven by robust demand from the HPC market. Quarterly revenue reached $40.2B, up 33.7% YoY, while gross margin climbed to 67.7%. Net income surged 77.4% YoY, setting a new company record.

Advanced Nodes Approach 80% of Revenue
TSMC announced that its 2nm process contributed wafer revenue for the first time in 2Q26, accounting for 3% of total wafer revenue. Combined with 3nm (30%), 5nm (33%), and 7nm (11%), technologies at 7nm and below represented 77% of total wafer revenue during the quarter.

The company also noted that, as 2nm remains in the capacity ramp-up phase, inventory days increased by seven days QoQ to 87 days.

Cost Optimization Offsets Overseas Expansion Pressure
TSMC attributed its 1.5 percentage-point QoQ improvement in gross margin to 67.7% primarily to internal cost optimization and higher capacity utilization. These gains were partially offset by the margin dilution associated with the ongoing expansion of overseas fabs. Capital expenditures totaled $15.7B during the quarter.

North America Remains TSMCs Largest Market
From an end-market perspective, HPC remained the primary growth driver, contributing 66% of quarterly revenue and growing 20% QoQ. Geographically, customers in North America accounted for 78% of total revenue, maintaining the region's position as TSMC's largest market.

text:
#Tower's recently announced $3 billion investment in #Japan centers on the former 12-inch Panasonic Semiconductor fab. The company's semiconductor assets were restructured following #Nuvoton's acquisition of Panasonic Semiconductor in 2020: Tower assumed the 12-inch specialty process and #SiPh platform, while Nuvoton took over the 8-inch #MCU, analog, and power semiconductor businesses. Tower is now leveraging the former Arai fab site while constructing additional capacity adjacent to its Uozu facility, positioning Japan as its global manufacturing hub for 12-inch SiPh.

Tower has cultivated its SiPh business for optical communications for many years and is already a key foundry partner for several of #China's leading optical module vendors. As AI-driven bandwidth demand continues to accelerate, Chinese optical module manufacturers have aggressively expanded production capacity in recent years. Many have also developed in-house SiPh IC design capabilities beyond building substantial domestic CW laser capacity. Against this backdrop, Tower is strengthening its SiPh manufacturing capacity through its 12-inch facilities in Japan to support growing customer demand.

Overall, Tower is capitalizing on Japan's existing manufacturing infrastructure, experienced workforce, and government incentives to rapidly scale 12-inch SiPh production. The company has already secured approximately $1.3 billion in SiPh revenue commitments for 2027 from major customers, along with $290 million in capacity prepayments. #TrendForce believes these commitments indicate that the Japanese expansion is not merely a speculative capacity investment, but one underpinned by firm customer demand and strong order visibility.
